page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 4.0 GB of RAM, providing a ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including avx512f and avx512_vnni), AES cryptography, and BMI2. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results position this instance primarily in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (1403.59) and multi-core (3699.56) CPU performance fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores are weak, with the memory score of 1052.97 placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show 27.14 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 22.64 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing represent moderate strengths, scoring in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local storage, the n2-highcpu-4 is designed for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and simple batch compilation tasks. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded processing due to its constrained 4.0 GB RAM capacity and lower multi-core benchmark efficiency. From a resource density perspective, it offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower entry point, but users must trade off raw multi-threaded throughput and memory capacity.
